Southern Yan defectors arrived—Zhong the prince of Beidi, Yi the prince of Jiyang, and Shi duke of Gaodu.

He sent Yao Bi, Lian Cheng, and Qifu Gangui with thirty thousand west against Nutan; Qi Nan led twenty thousand horse against Helian Bobo.

Helian Bobo hugged the northern bends.
Helian Bobo withdrew to hold the river bend.
勃勃退保河曲 means Bobo withdrew (退) to defend (保) the river bend (河曲); 'hugged' obscures the retreat and 'northern' is not in the source.
Yao Shang and Wang Min marched twenty thousand east; Jin retired.
Yao Shang and Wang Min marched with twenty thousand to his rescue; Jin retired.
The source (率眾二萬救之) says they led twenty thousand to save Qiao Zong; no direction is stated, so 'east' is unsupported.
Wei Hua draped Qiao Zong in nine tinsel honors and kingly seals aping Wei-Jin ritual.
Wei Hua, bearing credentials, invested Qiao Zong as grand commander-in-chief, chief minister, and King of Shu with the nine bestowals, following Wei-Jin precedent.
The idiomatic drops the appointments 大都督、相國、蜀王 given in the literal and misrenders 九錫 (the nine bestowals) as 'nine tinsel honors'.

Right Vice Director Wei Hua and others remonstrated, saying, "If the Chariot-and-Cavalry General moves lightly, he will collapse without battle, and he may not even reach Wei’s camp. May Your Majesty consider it."

Right Vice Director Wei Hua and others remonstrated, saying, "If Your carriage and cavalry move lightly, they will surely collapse without a battle, and may not even reach Manwei’s camp. May Your Majesty consider it."
車騎輕動 refers to Xing's own carriage and cavalry moving lightly (cf. 車駕動軫 in s0048 and 輕如嵬營 in s0044), not to a Chariot-and-Cavalry General; 嵬營 is Manwei's camp, not 'Wei's camp'.

Right Vice Director Wei Hua and others remonstrated, saying, "If the carriage and cavalry move lightly, they will surely collapse of themselves without fighting, and Manwei’s camp may not be reachable either. May Your Majesty consider it."
車騎輕動 refers to Xing's own carriage and cavalry moving lightly (cf. 車駕動軫 in s0048 and 輕如嵬營 in s0044), not to a Chariot-and-Cavalry General; 嵬營 is Manwei's camp, not 'Wei's camp'.

Huan Qian camped at Zhijiang; Gou Lin camped at Jiangjin.

Huan Qian's noble name seduced wavering Jin troops.
Huan Qian came from a noble family east of the Yangzi whose retainers were spread throughout Jing and Chu, so the Jin officers and soldiers all harbored thoughts of defecting.
The idiomatic omits 江左貴族 and 部曲遍于荊、楚 (his retinues filled Jing and Chu) and understates 晉之將士皆有叛心.
Gou Lin took fright and withdrew.
苟林懼而引歸 says Gou Lin feared and withdrew; 'upstream' is not in the source and 懼 is omitted.
Qifu Gangui stormed Jincheng and took Ren Lan.
Qifu Gangui rebelled with his host, stormed Jincheng, and seized its prefect Ren Lan.
The idiomatic omits 以眾叛 (rebelled with his host) and 太守 (Ren Lan was the prefect).
Yao Xing promoted Bi to minister of education, attendant-in-ordinary, and grand general.
Yao Xing promoted Bi to Director of the Secretariat, attendant-in-ordinary, and grand general.
尚書令 is the Director of the Secretariat; 'minister of education' renders 司徒, a different office (as in s0008 and s0034 of this chapter).
At this Xing appointed Bi minister of education, palace attendant, grand general.
At this Xing appointed Bi Director of the Secretariat, palace attendant, grand general.
尚書令 is the Director of the Secretariat; 'minister of education' renders 司徒, a different office (as in s0008 and s0034 of this chapter).
Yao Xing spurned Bi and sent Suo Leng to coax Gangui.
Yao Xing did not follow this advice; he made his Grand Master of Ceremonies Suo Leng Grand Commandant, concurrently Interior Secretary of Longxi, to win over Gangui.
興不從 means Xing did not follow Guo Bo's recommendation (it does not name Bi), and the idiomatic omits Suo Leng's offices 太常, 太尉 and 領隴西內史.
Liang Guoer banqueted inside his living tomb west of Pingliang.

At that time Liang Guoer, a Western Hu at Pingliang, built himself a tomb while still alive; he often took his wives and concubines into it to feast, and when drunk he climbed onto the spirit couch and sang.
西胡 is Liang Guoer's ethnonym (Western Hu), not 'west of Pingliang'; the idiomatic also drops the wives and concubines and the singing on the spirit couch.
He died past eighty a decorated frontier general.
Having repeatedly won great merit on campaigns, he was made General Who Guards the North by Xing and enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyu; he died aged over eighty.
The idiomatic omits Xing's appointment of him as 鎮北將軍 and the barony 平輿男 stated in the source.
Yang Sheng of Chouchi struck toward Qishan.
Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, rebelled and raided Qishan.
仇池公楊盛叛 says the Duke of Chouchi rebelled (叛); the idiomatic omits both the rebellion and the title.

Twenty-four late ministers joined sacrifices at Yao Chang's shrine.

He also issued an edict that the former chief minister Yao Xu, grand tutor Yao Shuode, grand mentor Yao Min, grand marshal Yao Chong, minister Yin Wei, and others, twenty-four in all, share in the sacrifices at Yao Chang's temple.
The idiomatic drops all five named honorees (姚緒、姚碩德、姚旻、姚崇、尹緯) and their offices given in the source and literal.
Yao Bi framed Wenzong before crown prince Hong.
Yao Wenzong enjoyed the favor of Yao Hong; Yao Bi hated him deeply and falsely accused Wenzong of resentful words, citing the attendant censor Lian Taosheng as witness.
The source says Wenzong was favored by 姚泓 and that 姚弼 slandered him with 廉桃生 as witness; 'framed before crown prince Hong' reverses Hong's role and drops Lian Taosheng.
Qiang mutiny near Er drew punitive columns.
At that time the Qiang of Er county rebelled against Xing, and Xing sent Rear General Liancheng, Garrison Army Peng Bailang, and North Gentleman-General Yao Luodu to punish them.
The idiomatic omits Xing and the three commanders 斂成、彭白狼、姚洛都 named in the source and literal.

The idiomatic drops the named memorialists 懿、恢、弟諶 and the target 弼; 'execution' overstates 請致之刑法 (deliver him to penal law).

He then appointed Xiuzhi General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Yangzhou, and Zongzhi and the others all received appointments.

Local militias squeezed Kang Huan until he surrendered.
Huang Jin and other men of Shangluo raised loyalist troops to flank Kang Huan, who then led his followers back to confess his guilt.
The idiomatic omits the named leader 黃金 (Huang Jin), given in the literal, and softens 歸罪 (returned confessing guilt).

晚乃為吏部令史 means he only late became a Personnel Bureau clerk; nothing in the source says he was demoted.

When Yao Chang fled to the horse pastures, Yin Wei, Yin Xiang, Pang Yan and others stirred up the local strongmen and made Yao Chang alliance chief, becoming foremost among the founding ministers.
